square/pairs: Self-attention scores every token against every token. T tokens make a T by T matrix: T squared scores. Four tokens, sixteen scores.
square/double: Double the tokens to eight, and there are sixty four scores: four times as many. Doubling T quadruples the scores.
square/linear: The queries, keys and values grow only in step with T: one row per token. And the weights do not grow at all.
memory/bytes: Each score is stored in two bytes. One score matrix for a thousand tokens is a million scores: two million bytes, two megabytes.
memory/long: At eight thousand tokens, it is sixty four million scores, one hundred twenty eight megabytes, for a single head.
memory/heads: And every head computes its own. With sixteen heads, one layer holds about two gigabytes of scores.
memory/why: That square is why long inputs are expensive for attention: twice the context, four times the work and memory.
